chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Rockland Palace skating barn versus Dunbar Palace nightclub
summary: The Rockland Palace was a huge barn for one-nighters and skating; the Dunbar Palace was a steady weekly nightclub job.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. I see. Then here it says, "Fletcher or Horace Henderson's Stompers, with a new personnel of Midwestern musicians, including Syd Valentine, Roy Eldridge, et cetera, reorganized in the fall of '28 on into '29 and 1930." That's just -- apparently what they're doing is they are stating these are five essentially different groups. Okay. Horace Henderson and his orchestra with the revamped personnel, Jack Butler, Sandy Williams, Rupert Cole, et cetera, at the Dunbar and Rockland Palaces.

The Rockland Palace, they are confusing. That was either at 155th or 158th and 8th Avenue, which was a huge barn which hired bands just for one nighters. It wasn't a steady thing, like a night club or one of those things. The Dunbar Palace was a night club.
(Unintelligible) It was a steady job, weekly.

The Rockland Palace is where they had roller skating, you know, and all that stuff going on there, so I don't know how they got that confused. Fletcher used to come up and play the Rockland Palace after the

Roseland. You know when you're finished at night? Sometimes they'd have a breakfast dance, and I've been up there with them when they played the breakfast dance, but it was only a one nighter, extra job. Good old Rockland Palace, skating rink.
